findings.finding: The root skill's own composes_with renders as 'Builds on: -' and 'Used by: -', which reads to a fresh composer as unused, directly contradicting its own description's claim that 'every other skill assumes this one is loaded' — every wave-1 skill lists agentic-stack under builds_on.
findings.evidence: "composes_with": {"builds_on": [], "used_by": []} in agentic-stack/skill.json, versus description: "Every other skill assumes this one is loaded."
findings.suggested_change: Populate used_by with the wave-1 skills that already declare builds_on: ["agentic-stack"], or add a one-line note next to the empty table explaining that the root skill is exempt from the manifest's symmetry check by design.

findings.finding: The row generalizes from a single LiteLLM routing quirk to a claim about 'de facto standards' in general; the cited fact never uses that framing and is about one hardcoded provider list, not standards drift, so origin=sourced overstates what the fact supports.
findings.evidence: Row text: "Assume a de facto standard can itself be shaped around one implementation: a widely adopted route in the substrate branches only on a fixed list of names and refuses a provider actually in use..." — F-a4-08 text is only: "Batch runs through Gemini's native `:batchGenerateContent` via LiteLLM passthrough — not the OpenAI-shaped `/v1/batches` route, which branches only on `openai`/`azure`/`vertex_ai` and refuses Gemini."
findings.suggested_change: Narrow the row to what F-a4-08 actually shows (one route hardcoded to three provider names refusing a fourth), or mark the generalization to 'de facto standards' as proposed and keep the fact only as its supporting example.

findings.finding: The mandatory differs_in_execution_model field is described three separate times in prose (an invariant and two instruction steps) but never given a formal shape/schema, unlike the sibling build-evidence-record skill which specifies its analogous field-set as a full JSON Schema. A fresh author building the proposed check_adapter_pairs.py tool has no concrete structure to validate against.
findings.evidence: instructions[3].action: "record the answer in a machine-readable differs_in_execution_model field on the pair, naming the axis and both values" — no accompanying contract.shapes entry exists anywhere in build-adapter-pair/skill.json (grep for "shapes" returns nothing).
findings.suggested_change: Add a contract.shapes entry (proposed) defining differs_in_execution_model as {axis: enum of the seven axes, today_value: string, second_value: string}, the way build-evidence-record's evidence-record shape does for its own required fields.

findings.finding: The instruction says a new layer prefix is needed only when 'none of the six existing ones (core, cap, xc, seam, compose, build) can hold the skill', but schemas/skill.schema.json's layer enum and tools/validate_skills.py's LAYERS dict both recognize a seventh layer, 'root' — the very layer agentic-stack itself uses. The instruction undercounts the taxonomy it is meant to police.
findings.evidence: instructions[10].action: "Add a new layer prefix only when none of the six existing ones (core, cap, xc, seam, compose, build) can hold the skill"; schemas/skill.schema.json layer enum is ["root", "core", "cap", "xc", "seam", "compose", "build"]; tools/validate_skills.py: LAYERS = {"root": None, "core": "core-", ...}.
findings.suggested_change: Say seven existing layers and name root alongside the other six, noting root is reserved for agentic-stack alone.

findings.finding: The skill inlines a full ~145-line JSON Schema directly in the contract and carries a 12-row instructions table, both exceeding build-skill-authoring's own progressive-disclosure rule ('roughly 3 to 10 rows per table' and 'move long material — a full schema... — into references/'), and unlike build-adapter-pair, build-evidence-record has no references/ directory at all.
findings.evidence: build-skill-authoring instructions[12].action: "hold to roughly 3 to 10 rows per table, and move long material (a full schema, a table of standards, worked examples) into references/"; build-evidence-record's Instructions table has 12 rows and its Shapes section embeds the complete evidence-record JSON Schema inline.
findings.suggested_change: Move the evidence-record JSON Schema into references/evidence-record.schema.json (cited by filename from the Shapes row) and split or trim the instructions table toward the stated 3-10 row budget.

findings.finding: All four wave-1 skills independently restate the same underlying fact (F-a7-03, the 9-stage pipeline that ran green with every behavioural stage skipped) as their own best-practice row instead of one skill stating it and the others citing it by name, contrary to build-skill-authoring's own best practice 'compose by name, not by copy... it never restates the neighbour's rows, so a change lands in one place.'
findings.evidence: F-a7-03 appears as a best_practices row in agentic-stack, build-adapter-pair, and build-skill-authoring, and as instructions[12] plus a best_practices row in build-evidence-record — four independent restatements of one fact within the same wave.
findings.suggested_change: Let agentic-stack (already builds_on for all three) hold the canonical statement and have the build-* skills reference it by name in their own row text rather than re-deriving the wording each time.

findings.finding: The description's first trigger clause, 'Load whenever you are about to write down a result', is broad enough to fire on nearly any assertion made anywhere in this repo, risking over-triggering relative to the skill's actual, narrower scope (the evidence-record shape and claimed/measured labelling).
findings.evidence: description: "Load whenever you are about to write down a result, label a check as passing, upgrade a claim to a measurement, cite evidence inside a skill, or reconcile a measurement that contradicts what the design says"
findings.suggested_change: Tighten the first clause to something like 'about to record a definition-of-done outcome or evidence-store entry' so it doesn't read as covering every written statement.

brief_improvements: Tell authors explicitly that layer 'root' exists and is reserved for agentic-stack, since build-skill-authoring's own instructions currently list only six layers and miss the one the root contract itself uses.

Add a rule to the author brief that a fact already stated by a skill under builds_on should be referenced by name rather than restated with new wording, since all four wave-1 skills independently re-derive F-a7-03.

Require any 'machine-readable field' named in an invariant or instruction (like differs_in_execution_model) to be backed by a contract.shapes entry in the same skill, the way build-evidence-record already does for its own record shape, so a fresh author has a schema to code against rather than only prose.

State the progressive-disclosure budget (3-10 rows/table, long material to references/) as a checked rule rather than a step 12 aside, since the skill that most needs it (build-evidence-record, with its inlined 145-line schema) currently doesn't follow it.
what_worked: Every sourced quote in all four skills verified as a true verbatim substring of its cited kb record — zero mechanical citation errors found across 73 sourced rows.

Definitions of done are honestly labelled: build-adapter-pair's is claimed because its tool genuinely doesn't exist yet (verified: tools/check_adapter_pairs.py is absent), while agentic-stack, build-evidence-record, and build-skill-authoring cite exact error strings that were confirmed present in the real tool source.
Provenance blocks (PASS.md sha256, kb chain heads) are identical across all four skills and match the current kb/meta.json exactly — no stale citations.

Design-rule-to-invariant mapping in agentic-stack (each of the seven B1 rules restated as a pass/fail test) is a clean, checkable translation that the other three skills correctly build on rather than re-deriving.
